title: Cleopas walks away from Jerusalem — Luke 24
paragraphs: Cleopas walks away from Jerusalem — Luke 24
He left the city where hope was supposed to win.
Cleopas walked away from Jerusalem with dust on his feet and disappointment in his chest.

Luke 24 is not just about a road.
It is about a heart in retreat.

Jesus had been crucified.
The tomb was already stirring with rumors.
But Cleopas was still leaving.
That’s the part that hits hard.

You can be close to the miracle…
and still walk in the wrong direction.

He had the reports.
He had the memories.
He had the story.
But grief can make a man abandon the very place where God is about to speak.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Jesus did not wait for Cleopas to find his way back.
He met him on the road.
In the confusion.
In the slow heartbreak.
In the questions that sounded more like surrender than faith.
That is the Gospel, beloved.

We do not climb our way back to Christ.
Christ comes near to us.

He listens.
He opens the Scriptures.
He breaks the bread.
And suddenly the eyes of a man walking away are opened by the Savior he almost missed.
Some of us are Cleopas right now.

Still talking about Jesus.
Still processing the pain.
Still moving our feet away from the place of promise.
But hear me.

Your disappointment is not stronger than His resurrection.
Your confusion is not louder than His voice.
Your detour is not beyond His reach.

The risen Christ still walks roads filled with shattered expectations.
And He still turns runaways into witnesses.

Cleopas left Jerusalem broken.
He returned burning.

That is what Jesus does.
He meets you in retreat and sends you back with fire.
